topic: Spotting emerging skills from usage data
angle: The best AI skill forecasts are bottom-up: watch real usage, then fund it.
sourceTitle: Spot New Tech Skills Emerging From the Workforce
linkedinPost:
Most reskilling plans are slideware. The skills that matter show up first in the work.

MIT Sloan Management Review highlights a smarter path: spot new tech skills emerging from the workforce itself. I’ve seen this beat top‑down forecasts every time.

Look for bottom‑up signals: spikes in tool usage, recurring “shadow workflows” in teams, and ad-hoc template sharing. That’s where real capability is being invented under pressure to deliver.

Operationalize it: instrument internal tools for anonymized pattern spotting, stand up micro-credentials tied to on-the-job artifacts, and fund just‑in‑time training sprints. Rotate early adopters as “internal instructors” for one quarter—it scales culture, not just content.

Metrics I trust: half‑life of training adoption (how long it stays used), time-to-first-impact on a real KPI, and reuse rate of internal prompts/templates.

Your AI transformation moves at the speed of the skills your people actually practice, not the skills you list.

How are you detecting emergent skills before they hit the HR catalog? #AITransformation #DigitalTransformation #EnterpriseAI
